title: Win32 suspended process + atomic JOB_LIST membership + assignment proof + resume
description:
SPIDR child 2a of 2, split from task-a02496064e9e4e87a888cc112830d7a4 by architect-5aba94da on plan shape. Human confirmed the split in the REPL before it was created.

WHY SPLIT, on plan shape and never on lines (epic rail 5): the single plan re-measured to 10 distinct affectedFiles and 12 steps -- BOTH exactly at the daemon hard ceiling, zero slack -- once three facts the parent could not have known were measured on disk. See MEASURED ON DISK below. Responsibilities are genuinely separable: this child builds a process INTO the Job; child 2b (task-TBD-2B) tears one down and proves it on real Windows.

MEASURED ON DISK at HEAD 025dc49 by architect-5aba94da, 2026-08-09. Re-measure before planning; these claims are stale by default like any other:
1. `grep -c '' src/win32.rs` => 252. Child 1's win32.rs ALREADY EXCEEDS the <=250 hard bar. Its own lib.rs:31 says "win32.rs sits at 246 of its 250-line target", which is no longer true. So win32.rs cannot absorb the process-side arms; it must be split first, and that split is work the parent task never budgeted.
2. `tests/job_sweep.rs:169` asserts `assert_eq!(produced, all)` where `all` is built from `NativeOp::ALL`. NativeOp is a closed enum with `pub const ALL: [NativeOp; 6]`. Adding ANY process-side variant breaks that existing test. Child 1's test file is a file this work must edit, and the parent description does not name it.
3. All 19 windows-sys symbols this work needs are present in the pinned `=0.61.2`: CreateProcessW, PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST, PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST, InitializeProcThreadAttributeList, UpdateProcThreadAttribute, DeleteProcThreadAttributeList, ResumeThread, GetProcessId, GetProcessTimes, QueryFullProcessImageNameW, WaitForSingleObject, GetExitCodeProcess, TerminateProcess, STARTUPINFOEXW, EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT, CREATE_SUSPENDED, CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT are all in Windows/Win32/System/Threading/mod.rs and need the `Win32_System_Threading` feature added to Cargo.toml (deliberately omitted by child 1). AssignProcessToJobObject and IsProcessInJob are in Windows/Win32/System/JobObjects/mod.rs and are ALREADY reachable under the enabled feature set.
4. Baseline gate is green: `cargo test --locked -p moe-windows-job-core` => 7 passed, 0 failed.

DEPENDS ON task-a24cb925a9a94002b805e9ccf1715978 (child 1), which is DONE and committed at HEAD. Reuse its crate, Win32Calls trait, NativeOp/NativeError/RawHandle vocabulary, OwnedHandle and Job unchanged. Do not recreate or fork them. Moving child 1's `#[cfg(windows)] mod system` block verbatim into its own file is a SPLIT, not a fork, and is explicitly sanctioned by child 1's lib.rs:31-35 ("new arms should arrive with a split by responsibility rather than by reformatting").

Objective: put a process inside the Job with no pre-assignment crash window, and prove it is really there before it is allowed to run a single instruction.

Deliverable, inside packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/:
- Cargo.toml: add the `Win32_System_Threading` feature to the existing exact-pinned windows-sys dependency. Confirm Cargo.lock is byte-unchanged by the feature addition rather than assuming it; commit it only if it genuinely changed.
- src/win32.rs: extract child 1's `#[cfg(windows)] mod system` block verbatim into src/system_job.rs (a pure move, zero logic edits), then add the construction-side NativeOp variants, extend NativeOp::ALL and its array length, and declare the process-side call-table trait. Must land <=250 lines.
- src/system_job.rs (NEW): child 1's moved job Win32Calls impl, unchanged.
- src/system_process.rs (NEW): the real windows-sys impl of the construction-side arms only.
- src/process.rs (NEW): the construction orchestration -- attribute-list prepare carrying PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST plus a three-handle inherited allowlist, CreateProcessW with CREATE_SUSPENDED, explicit lpApplicationName and a Unicode environment, then the explicit AssignProcessToJobObject confirmation, membership proof, live-handle identity proof, and ResumeThread asserting a prior suspend count of exactly 1.
- src/lib.rs: module declarations and re-exports.
- tests/job_sweep.rs: repair the NativeOp::ALL cross-check WITHOUT weakening it. It must still fail if a job arm goes unreached; it must not be softened into a subset test that would pass while an arm is dead.
- tests/process_sweep.rs (NEW): the injected-call-table sweep over construction arms.

The atomic JOB_LIST membership removes the pre-assignment crash window; the explicit AssignProcessToJobObject call preserves the separately testable assign-failure arm. Supported floor is Windows 10 / Server 2016. This host is win32 x64, so this is honestly buildable and testable here.

NOT IN SCOPE, and owned by child 2b: wait, exit query, terminate, ActiveProcesses==0 query, the full reverse-order unwind protocol (terminate-and-await a child that was already created), and tests/real_windows.rs. This child owns only the narrower RAII obligation on its own failure paths: close every handle it acquired exactly once and delete the attribute list exactly once. Also NOT in scope: Node/stdio framing, JavaScript hostile-input validation, Claude discovery/grants, daemon/store authority, receipts, or any public @moe/runner export.

Production consumer: task-af3d7bc8af2146cf92d98557ed0e90c0 (Windows Job broker protocol), then task-4d1f8ba54cb6476c930c46b413f882aa.

Every construction failure path closes every acquired handle exactly once and deletes the attribute list exactly once, verified by a per-handle close-count table across all cases; the FIRST error survives cleanup rather than being overwritten by a cleanup outcome; and a close whose outcome is unknown is returned as an error rather than converted to success.

NativeError still carries only the closed operation enum and a numeric Win32 code. No executable path, argv, cwd, environment or raw handle value is reachable from it or from any Debug impl -- RawHandle still has no Debug. The locked test and release-build commands both exit 0 with no committed target, executable, debug or probe artifact.
taskRails: Use the Windows 10+/Server 2016+ PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST crash-atomic membership path, followed by the explicit AssignProcessToJobObject confirmation, and only then the membership proof before resume.

Native failures carry a closed operation enum and numeric Win32 error only; never echo executable, argv, cwd, environment, or raw handle values. Adding a Debug derive to a type holding a RawHandle must stay a compile error.

Keep every Rust production source focused, target and hard-cap <=250 physical lines; split before 400. Commit Cargo.lock only if it genuinely changed, and never commit Cargo target output or binaries.
This is a native primitive, not authority: no @moe/runner root export, Claude policy, activation grant, daemon/store call, or evidence claim.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN. Create src/process.rs holding the construction orchestration generic over `C: Win32Calls + ProcessCalls`, reusing child 1's OwnedHandle for every acquired handle and child 1's Job unchanged. Sequence, in this exact order: initialize the attribute list for two attributes; set PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST carrying the Job; set PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST carrying exactly the three caller-supplied inheritable handles; CreateProcessW with CREATE_SUSPENDED | EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT | CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT, an explicit lpApplicationName and a UTF-16 double-NUL-terminated environment block; then the explicit AssignProcessToJobObject; then the membership proof; then the live-handle identity proof (pid and creation time); and only then ResumeThread. Two refusals are OURS and carry code 0, following child 1's convention at job.rs:78 — a membership query that succeeds but reports false, and a resume that succeeds but reports a prior suspend count other than exactly 1. A membership or resume call that itself fails carries the real GetLastError instead; these are four distinct outcomes and must not collapse into two. The attribute list is deleted exactly once on every path, success and failure alike, and the first error always survives cleanup. Note the type-level constraint the storage must satisfy: UpdateProcThreadAttribute stores a pointer to its lpvalue rather than copying it, so the job handle and the handle array must be owned by the same value that owns the attribute list and must not move before CreateProcessW returns. This step makes step 5's ordering test pass.

GREEN. Step 5's ordering test passes. 8 tests total: 7 job_sweep + 1 process_sweep, exit 0.

src/process.rs now holds `ContainedProcess<'c, C: Win32Calls + ProcessCalls>` reusing child 1's OwnedHandle for both acquired handles and child 1's Job. Sequence enforced in exactly the plan's order and pinned by the whole-vector assertion: init_attribute_list(2) -> set_job_list_attribute -> set_handle_list_attribute(spec.inherited) -> create_process_suspended -> assign_process_to_job -> prove_membership -> process_id -> creation_time -> resume.

FOUR DISTINCT OUTCOMES, NOT TWO, on both proof arms:
- membership CALL fails => `?` propagates the real Win32 code on NativeOp::IsProcessInJob.
- membership call SUCCEEDS reporting false => NativeError::new(NativeOp::IsProcessInJob, 0), child 1's code-0 "this refusal is ours" convention from job.rs:78.
- resume CALL fails => real Win32 code on NativeOp::ResumeThread.

THE FOUR EASY-TO-GET-WRONG SPECIFICS, each handled explicitly:
- InitializeProcThreadAttributeList two-call size probe: the first call passes a null list and a zero size and its BOOL is DELIBERATELY NOT checked, because failing with ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER is its documented success mode; treating it as an error would refuse every construction. What IS checked is `probed != 0 || size == 0` — a probe that unexpectedly succeeds, or reports no size, refuses rather than allocating nothing. The buffer is `Vec<usize>`, not `Vec<u8>`: the list needs pointer alignment and a byte vector only guarantees alignment 1. Sized by `size.div_ceil(size_of::<usize>())`, allocated once, never grown, so the heap block never moves.
- CreateProcessW is passed bInheritHandles = 1 (TRUE). With FALSE the HANDLE_LIST allowlist is honoured by inheriting nothing and the child comes up with no standard streams — invisible until a real process runs. Flags are CREATE_SUSPENDED | EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT | CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT; lpApplicationName is explicit (never null, which is what removes the unquoted-path search); the environment is the caller's double-NUL UTF-16 block; STARTUPINFOEXW.cb is sizeof(STARTUPINFOEXW) and dwFlags carries STARTF_USESTDHANDLES with the three handles also named in StartupInfo, since allowlisting alone does not assign them. lpCommandLine gets a MUTABLE COPY — CreateProcessW may write through it.
- ResumeThread is NOT a BOOL check. It returns the PRIOR suspend count with u32::MAX as the failure signal; read as a BOOL, the ordinary count 1 would read as success and 0 as failure.
- IsProcessInJob's two results are read separately: the returned BOOL is call success, the answer arrives through the out-pointer. `check(...)?` runs FIRST so a failed call can never have its uninitialised answer read.

THE POINTER-LIFETIME FOOTGUN IS CLOSED BY TYPE. UpdateProcThreadAttribute stores a POINTER to lpvalue rather than copying it. OwnedAttributeList therefore owns `job: Box<HANDLE>` and `handles: Box<[HANDLE; 3]>` alongside the buffer, so their addresses are fixed on the heap even if the list value itself moves. A `&local` or a moved Vec here would compile, pass every scripted test (the double dereferences nothing) and be a use-after-free on real Windows — the module doc says so, in those words.

HELPER REUSE — a deliberate, disclosed re-declaration. as_handle/last_error/check are re-declared `pub(super)` in system_process.rs instead of imported from system_job.rs, because DoD item 1 requires system_job.rs to stay BYTE-IDENTICAL to child 1's committed block and widening its private helpers would break the verbatim diff. They follow child 1's pattern character for character rather than introducing a second error-handling style.

2. system_process.rs is the file most likely to breach 250 lines; the attribute-list arm alone needs a two-call size probe, a correctly aligned owned buffer, and a JOB handle whose storage must outlive CreateProcessW. Do not instead compress by deleting SAFETY comments.

3. ATTRIBUTE LIFETIME IS THE REAL FOOTGUN. UpdateProcThreadAttribute stores a POINTER to lpvalue; it does not copy. The job handle passed for JOB_LIST and the handle array passed for HANDLE_LIST must both stay alive and un-moved until CreateProcessW returns. A local temporary or a moved Vec here is a use-after-free that will pass every scripted test in this task, because the double never dereferences anything. Own that storage inside the same struct that owns the attribute list.

4. bInheritHandles must be TRUE for PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST to mean anything, and every handle in the allowlist must itself be inheritable. An allowlist passed with bInheritHandles FALSE silently inherits nothing and the child gets no stdio -- invisible until 2b runs a real process.

5. IsProcessInJob has two failure modes that must NOT collapse: the call failing (BOOL 0 -> NativeOp::IsProcessInJob with GetLastError) versus the call succeeding while reporting false (-> NativeOp::IsProcessInJob with code 0, our refusal). Both must be separately tested; a single test asserting "membership refused" satisfies neither the global rail nor DoD item 4. Same shape for ResumeThread: u32::MAX is a Win32 failure, a successful call returning a prior count other than 1 is our refusal with code 0.

6. The order test must assert the FULL recorded call sequence with assert_eq! on the whole vector, exactly as child 1's successful_creation_calls_create_set_query_in_order does. A test that only asserts resume appears after membership can pass with an entire step missing.
